habitat_summary: Pelagic fish in moderately cold coastal waters.
temperature_note: Peru field seasonal temperatures: 14-18 C in winter and 16-23 C in summer; observations, not thermal limits or optimum.
season_note: Spawning occurs nearly year-round, strongest in August-September and February-March.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE reports distribution changes during warm 2023 conditions in the northern Humboldt Current region.
peru_coast_range_note: Northern Humboldt Current region of Peru.
fishery_note: Industrial and artisanal fisheries are reported.
notes: No thermal optimum reported. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources. Existing season and El Nino references are present; remote recheck: no accesible (timeout or 502).

habitat_summary: Neritic to oceanic; epipelagic to mesopelagic. Two tagged animals moved from near-surface to deep daytime waters.
temperature_note: Peru observations span about 14 C at 50 m to 27.5 C at sea surface; different depths, not thermal limits.
season_note: IMARPE reports main spawning from October to January and secondary activity in August.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE survey reports a negative El Nino effect; 2018 bilingual abstracts differ in depth wording.
peru_coast_range_note: Peru, 10 to more than 500 nautical miles offshore.
fishery_note: IMARPE reports artisanal and industrial fleets.
notes: Two tagged squid reached 1200 m (2017, p. 174); this is not a population limit. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources. Existing season and El Nino references are present; remote recheck: no accesible (timeout or 502).

habitat_summary: Benthic in semi-protected bays on sedimentary bottoms; also sandy or muddy bottoms with shells and macroalgae.
temperature_note: Lab juveniles were tested at 17 and 22 C in Peru; treatment temperatures, not limits or optimum.
season_note: Spawning occurs year-round, stronger September to May.
el_nino_response_note: An IMARPE 2024 assessment reports poor population condition after the 2023-24 warm event despite expected density increase.
notes: Section 2.7.2 reports typical 5-40 m; IMARPE species record gives a broader intertidal-to-95 m distribution. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources. Machine-readable species landings pending: public monthly charts verified in F26; data endpoint not verified.

habitat_summary: Rocky intertidal and subtidal habitat; shelters in crevices and beneath rocks.
temperature_note: Field seasonal sea-surface averages in Ancash, Peru (2014-2023): 18.5-21.7 C; not thermal limits or optimum.
season_note: Spawning occurs year-round, with spring and summer peaks.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE diet observations during 1982-83 and 1997-98 El Nino differed by site; no coast-wide response inferred.

notes: Species record gives intertidal to 30 m. Review status: Landing workbook verified by common-name label and maritime row; continuous species coverage and scientific-name mapping need review; no thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources.

habitat_summary: Benthodemersal; IMARPE assessment reports concentrations at 100-200 m.
temperature_note: Peru field bottom temperatures: 10-16 C on normal cruise and 14.5-22.3 C during El Nino; not limits or optimum.
season_note: Main spawning in winter-spring; secondary spawning in summer-autumn.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE reports inverted distribution and 14.5-22.3 C bottom temperatures in the 1983 El Nino cruise.
notes: WoRMS accepts Merluccius peruanus; Merluccius gayi peruanus is retained as historical synonym. Review status: A closed published upper depth of 800 m is documented in F41; the original guide wording remains in depth_note.
depth_note: The guide records depths from 50 m to more than 600 m; no closed maximum is given. F41 states the species can be caught from near the surface to 800 m depth (fishing depth range).

habitat_summary: Pelagic-neritic fish in warm-temperate coastal waters over sandy or muddy bottoms.
temperature_note: Northern Peru bottom-trawl cruises in 1981-1988 recorded 14.2-17.2 C in normal years and 16.3-22.4 C during El Nino. These are bottom-temperature observations, not limits; compare only with bottom measurements in the same setting.
season_note: Higher reproductive activity and landings occur in spring and summer.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE reports higher cachema catches in Ancash and Lima during the 1997-98 El Nino; historical observation.
peru_coast_range_note: Peruvian coastal waters; source describes a northern-central Peru fishery.
fishery_note: Coastal fishery; landings reported from artisanal monitoring and PRODUCE records.
notes: Bottom temperatures from northern Peru cruises are now sourced from F42; they are observations, not limits. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources; existing season and El Nino notes are retained and the new 165 m and 154 m cruise-depth records differ from the existing 50 m endpoint.
depth_note: IMARPE gives 0-50 m. FishBase lists a depth range of 10 m to an unknown limit (Ref. 9118).

temperature_note: Peru catches below 100 m during El Nino were recorded at 15-20 C across depth levels; these are observations, not limits. This mixed-depth range must not be compared with surface temperature.
season_note: Main spawning occurs in winter and spring, with secondary spawning in summer.
el_nino_response_note: During strong El Nino events, schools were recorded at 100-200 m. This is an observed depth shift in Peru, not a forecast.
fishery_note: Industrial and artisanal fisheries are reported.
landing_data_source: PRODUCE artisanal landing workbook (common-name labels; maritime rows only)
landing_data_years: 2013-2025 (catalogue period; continuous species coverage not checked)
notes: Review status: Landing workbook verified by common-name label and maritime row; continuous species coverage and scientific-name mapping need review. No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources.
depth_note: Observed schools span 0-75 m during strong upwelling, 100-200 m during strong El Nino and 0-300 m with a stronger southern Cromwell extension. These are condition-specific distribution records, not species limits.

season_note: IMARPE reports higher artisanal landings in spring and summer. This describes landings, not spawning season.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE links the high landing records in 1983, 1987 and 1998 to El Nino. This historical landing association does not establish a change in stock size.
fishery_note: Industrial and artisanal fisheries are reported.

habitat_summary: Neritic pelagic fish that forms schools.
season_note: Spawning can occur throughout the year, with the main reproductive period from November to March. IMARPE reports the historical peak in January.
el_nino_response_note: During the 2015 El Nino in Lambayeque, large summer landings coincided with the arrival of equatorial surface waters. This is a local landing observation, not a change in stock size.
peru_coast_range_note: Reported from Costa Rica and Ecuador through Peru to Valparaiso, Chile, and the Galapagos.
fishery_note: Industrial and artisanal fisheries are reported.

habitat_summary: Epipelagic, neritic fish associated with Humboldt Current waters.
season_note: Spawning occurs year-round, mainly in October-December and February-March.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE reports juvenile sardine and samasa in the diet during El Nino events.
peru_coast_range_note: Distribution extends from Puerto Pizarro, Peru, to Talcahuano, Chile.
fishery_note: Industrial and artisanal fisheries are reported.

habitat_summary: Benthopelagic fish on shallow sandy and sandy-rocky continental shelf bottoms.
temperature_note: Northern Peru bottom-trawl cruises in 1981-1988 recorded 14.1-16.7 C in normal years and 14.8-21.2 C during El Nino. These are bottom-temperature observations, not limits; compare only with bottom measurements in the same setting.
season_note: The main spawning peak is in autumn; the Huacho cold-period study recorded a spring 1996 peak.
el_nino_response_note: The 1997-98 warm period negatively affected reproduction in the Huacho study.
peru_coast_range_note: Reported from Ecuador and Puerto Pizarro, Peru, to Corral, Chile.

depth_note: The factsheet gives 5-50 m; bottom-trawl records reach 140 m in normal years and 222 m during El Nino. These sources describe different settings and are kept as a disagreement.
